frontMatter.introduction:
Praveen Laboratories is a research-driven contract organization and Active Pharmaceutical Ingredient (API) manufacturer that delivers high-quality pharmaceutical and chemical services. The company is committed to scientific excellence, regulatory compliance, and client satisfaction. This Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) Manual has been developed to ensure consistent practices across departments and to uphold the highest standards of safety, quality, and operational efficiency.

This manual serves as a guiding framework for all employees, managers, and technical personnel involved in various functions at Praveen Laboratories. It outlines documented procedures, promotes regulatory alignment, and reinforces a culture of accountability and continuous improvement within the organization.
frontMatter.objective:
The primary objective of this SOP Manual is to:
Define uniform procedures and best practices across all operations at Praveen Laboratories.
Ensure compliance with applicable regulatory requirements such as Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP), ISO standards, and environmental norms.
Minimize process variability and enhance the quality, safety, and efficiency of services delivered.
Provide clear guidance to all staff for performing their tasks with consistency and accuracy.
Serve as a foundational reference for audits, inspections, training, and quality control.

sections.title: 5R Approach for Waste Reduction in API Manufacturing

blocks.text: Praveen Laboratories applies the 5R strategy — Reduce, Reuse, Recycle, Recovery, and Repurpose — to drive sustainable production practices, minimize environmental footprint, and improve process economics across its API manufacturing lifecycle.

sections.title: 5R Approach for Waste Reduction in API Manufacturing

body.text: Optimized Process Chemistry: Synthesis routes are selected during R&D based on their atom economy, yield efficiency, and minimal generation of by-products, reducing downstream waste. Real-Time Monitoring: In-line sensors and PAT tools (e.g., pH, IR, temp) help monitor critical process parameters and reduce the chances of batch failure or reprocessing, thereby lowering chemical and energy waste. Inventory Optimization: Raw materials and solvents are procured in calculated volumes, following FEFO principles and digital stock tracking, minimizing expiration and spoilage-related waste. Dry Cleaning Preference: Mechanical and dry cleaning methods (e.g., air jets, vacuuming) are preferred before wet cleaning of equipment to reduce effluent generation. Process Optimization for Waste Reduction: We continuously undertakes structured process optimization to minimize raw material use, energy input, and waste output across all production stages. Strategies include simplification of synthesis pathways to reduce intermediate steps, transition to high-efficiency reactors and utility systems, and deployment of advanced control systems for real-time process adjustment. Batch planning is streamlined through lean manufacturing principles, minimizing idle time, changeover losses, and partial batches. These collective measures significantly reduce generation of off-spec products, solvent consumption, and associated emissions, thereby enhancing both operational efficiency and environmental performance.

Solvent Reuse in Cleaning: IPA, acetone, and toluene recovered from cleaning operations are tested for purity and reused in initial rinse cycles for reactors and pipelines. Reusable Containers: Non-contaminated HDPE carboys, once emptied, are thoroughly washed, QC-checked, and reused internally for transferring utility fluids and non-hazardous solutions. Reusable Secondary Packaging: Thermocol, bubble wrap, and pallet covers from incoming materials are collected and reused for internal shipments and cushioning during in-house transfers. Reusable PPE in Non-GMP Areas: Cleanroom garments and goggles used in non-critical areas are cleaned and reused through validated laundering processes.

Segregated Recycling Zones: Each department maintains dedicated bins for paper, plastic, metal, and glass, ensuring uncontaminated segregation for easy dispatch to authorized recyclers. Metallic Scrap Recovery: Reactor internals, worn-out valves, dismantled frames, and scrap piping are sent for metal recycling through licensed scrap vendors. Paper & Admin Waste: Office-generated paper waste from documentation and packaging cartons are baled and sent to local recyclers monthly. QC Glassware Disposal: Damaged or expired glass vials and pipettes from the QC lab are decontaminated, crushed, and directed for glass recycling.

Solvent Distillation Units: Multi-stage distillation systems recover high-purity solvents, which are reused within the same product line or repurposed for plant cleaning operations. Energy Recovery from Waste Heat: Reactor and distillation unit jackets are integrated with heat exchangers to transfer residual heat to preheat incoming utilities like boiler feed water. Mother Liquor Re-entry: In selected processes, validated mother liquors containing residual APIs or intermediates are reused in the next crystallization stage to improve yield and reduce waste volume. ETP Sludge Co-processing: Filtered and dried sludge with fuel value is sent to cement industries for co-processing, avoiding landfill and utilizing its calorific potential. Wastewater Recovery: Treated effluent from STP/ETP is reused in cooling towers, floor washing, or utility purposes wherever compliance allows.

Damaged Barrels as Collection Bins: Leaky or deformed drums that cannot be reused for storage are converted into labeled collection bins for solid or segregated wastes. Scrap Wood Reuse in Maintenance: Discarded wooden pallets are cut and reused in the maintenance department for creating tool racks, supports, and wooden shims. Obsolete Equipment for Demo Use: Decommissioned lab and plant equipment is repurposed as demonstration units in training labs for technical staff and apprentices.

blocks.text: Praveen Laboratories actively integrates circular economy principles into its hazardous waste management framework by prioritizing the recovery and reuse of valuable input materials and shifting toward eco-friendly alternatives wherever technically feasible.

body.text:
Solvent Reclamation Units (SRUs) are installed in production blocks and QC labs. Spent solvents like IPA, methanol, ethyl acetate, and toluene are collected in dedicated drums and processed through multi-stage distillation units.
Mother liquors from crystallization processes are analyzed and reused based on API stability profiles, especially in early-stage reactions.
Recovered silica and charcoal from filtration units are dried, tested for reusability, and reused in subsequent filtration steps where purity allows.
Side stream reuse from continuous processes (e.g., purge streams containing residual active) are captured and reintegrated via feedback loops after QC clearance.
Wash solvents from intermediate cleaning stages are collected and analyzed for cross-contamination risk; if within control limits, they are reused in non-critical washing applications.
Excess buffer solutions and pH-adjusted aqueous streams are recovered and reused in utilities or cleaning-in-place (CIP) operations after quality checks.

Green chemistry audits are performed annually to identify process steps that can be modified to use biodegradable solvents or less toxic reagents.
Citric acid, sodium citrate, and ascorbic acid are adopted as neutralizing agents in place of hydrochloric or sulfuric acid during equipment cleaning cycles.
Bio-based cleaners and low-VOC surface disinfectants are used in non-critical plant areas (e.g., warehouses and corridors).
Plant-derived co-solvents like ethyl lactate are evaluated for use in API crystallization and granulation stages where compatibility permits.
Phosphate-free detergents and enzyme-based degreasers are introduced in CIP cycles to minimize aquatic toxicity.
Water-based degreasing agents are adopted for equipment and tool cleaning in maintenance workshops to replace petroleum-based solvents.
Preference is given to GMP-compliant suppliers who provide materials in recyclable or reusable packaging (returnable drums, collapsible IBCs).

steps.heading: Use of Alternative and Less Hazardous Substances

body.text:
Wherever feasible, Class 1 and Class 2 solvents are substituted with Class 3 solvents as per ICH guidelines to reduce health and environmental risks.
Halogenated compounds are phased out from synthetic pathways unless technically unavoidable, with alternatives vetted through a risk-benefit and performance matrix.
Process modifications are implemented to replace reagents with high GHS hazard categories (acute toxicity, skin sensitization) with safer analogues such as enzymatic catalysts or aqueous-based systems.
In high-temperature reactions, mineral acids are replaced with solid acid catalysts or ionic liquids to reduce corrosive emissions and hazardous effluent.

The procurement team follows a structured substitution-first policy, wherein vendor selection prioritizes suppliers offering less hazardous substitutes certified under globally recognized green chemistry or REACH compliance standards.
Procurement contracts mandate assessment of material hazard classifications, environmental fate, and life cycle impacts during the sourcing stage.
Supplier performance reviews include sustainability and hazard reduction metrics as core evaluation criteria, promoting long-term collaboration with environmentally responsible vendors.

blocks.text: Proper identification, safe containment, and compliant movement of hazardous waste are essential for minimizing the risk of chemical exposure, spills, fire, environmental damage, and legal non-compliance. Praveen Laboratories has established rigorous protocols aligned with the Hazardous and Other Wastes (Management and Transboundary Movement) Rules, 2016 and other applicable standards to ensure operational and regulatory control.

body.text:
Each hazardous waste container—drum, carboy, IBC, or bag—is labeled at the point of generation and remains traceable until final disposal.

Labelling Standards: All hazardous substances must be labeled in full compliance with GHS (Globally Harmonized System) or BIS (Bureau of Indian Standards). Labels must include:

Label Requirements (Printed, laminated, weatherproof):

Material/Waste Stream Name (e.g., Spent IPA, ETP Sludge)
Chemical Composition / Primary Hazardous Constituents
Physical State (solid/liquid/sludge/gas)
Hazard Class Symbols: Flammable, Corrosive, Toxic, Reactive (GHS-compatible)
Generator Department & Contact Person
Accumulation Start Date & Storage Expiry Limit (Max 90 days)
Waste Quantity: Gross weight, net weight, and tare weight
Disposal Method: (e.g., TSDF/Incineration/Recovery)
Container No. and Barcode

Label Implementation Notes:

All labels are bilingual (English + local language).
The Waste Manifest Management System (WMMS) logs each barcode into the centralized EHS database.
Labels are color-coded:
Red Border – Toxic Waste
Orange Border – Flammable Waste
Yellow Border – Reactive Waste
Black Border – Corrosive Waste

In case of container reuse (e.g., drum washing), old labels are removed, destroyed, and reissued to prevent incorrect identification.

Hazardous waste is stored in dedicated, secure, and well-equipped storage yards designed to eliminate cross-contamination, accidental mixing, and environmental exposure.

Physical Infrastructure: Acid- and Alkali-Resistant Flooring: Coated concrete with chemical-resistant epoxy.

Bund Walls: 110% secondary containment for the largest container in each storage area.
Flame Detectors & Smoke Sensors: Linked to the central fire alarm system.
Access Control: RFID-based entry system limited to trained personnel only.
Intrinsically Safe Lighting: Spark-proof fittings in flammable zones.
Segregation Protocols:
Operational Practices:

Containers are placed above ground level using polymer pallets.
FIFO Protocol: Clearly tagged with accumulation start date; wastes exceeding 90 days are reported to SPCB.
Daily Inspection Log: Includes label integrity, leakage signs, corrosion, and pest control status.
Visual indicators (arrows, area maps, GHS signage) are posted throughout the yard.

To prevent chemical burns, inhalation risk, reactivity, or ergonomic injury, strict handling procedures are enforced.

Personnel Qualification:

Only certified staff (trained in the Hazardous Waste Handling Module) may handle hazardous waste.

Training includes:

Correct PPE use
Material compatibility
Emergency spill response
Fire safety procedures

Transportation of hazardous waste from the generation area to storage, and from storage to final disposal is executed with maximum safety and full legal compliance.

Internal Transfer (Within Premises):

Use of anti-static, corrosion-resistant trolleys.
Waste containers are:
Secured with bungee cords/lid locks
Covered with polyethylene sheets if odor/vapor potential exists
Movement conducted only during non-peak hours to reduce interaction with production activities.
Transfer routes are pre-mapped and marked with directional indicators.
External Transfer (To TSDF/Co-Processing Facility):

Carried out only via SPCB-Authorized Transporters.
EHS prepares Form 10 Manifest in six copies, signed and stamped.
Containers loaded onto:
GPS-enabled covered trucks with flame-retardant tarpaulin
UN-approved sealed containers (with hazard placards)
Loaded with spill kits, MSDS folder, and emergency contact list
Disposal receipt with weight reconciliation is collected at the TSDF and uploaded to the EHS compliance portal within 48 hours.

All transport vehicles must be fitted with the following safety equipment and protocols:
ABC-type fire extinguishers (minimum 4 kg) placed near the driver’s cabin and rear of the vehicle.
Spill containment kits suitable for the class of waste being transported.
Proper ventilation systems, especially for VOC-generating wastes.
GPS-based tracking systems integrated with the site EHS dashboard for real-time shipment monitoring.
In the event of a road accident, leakage, or fire during transportation:

The Emergency Response Plan is immediately activated by the Transport Team.
Primary actions include:
Securing the perimeter and avoiding ignition sources.
Using spill kits to contain and neutralize the leaked substance.
Deploying personal protective equipment (PPE) as per the waste class.
Secondary actions involve:
Notifying local authorities, fire department, and the nearest hospital.
Informing the EHS Head and initiating incident documentation.
Post-incident, a Root Cause Analysis (RCA) is conducted, and incident records are retained in the Incident Register.

Transport logbook includes:
Transporter name and license number
Vehicle number and route taken
Time of departure and arrival
Container barcode numbers and weights
Records are retained for minimum 5 years in line with Praveen Laboratories’ data retention policy.

sections.title: Specialized Treatment & Safe Disposal of Hazardous Substances

body.text:
pH Neutralization Units have been installed in production and utility areas to treat acidic and alkaline rinses generated during equipment washing and cleaning activities. These units are automatically monitored for pH ranges and are equipped with acid/alkali dosing systems to bring effluent within neutral discharge standards before routing it to the Effluent Treatment Plant (ETP).
Double-stage Distillation Columns are utilized to process solvent waste that contains multiple impurities, especially from multistep synthesis batches. The first stage focuses on bulk recovery while the second ensures purification. Recovered solvents are sent for quality testing and reused for non-critical rinses or cleaning operations, reducing procurement of fresh solvent.
Activated Carbon Filtration Systems are installed at wastewater discharge points from QC and production areas to capture residual organics, color, and trace solvents. This filtration stage ensures that final rinse water is free from toxicants before entering the STP (Sewage Treatment Plant).

All hazardous wastes that cannot be recovered, reused, or treated in-house are sent to State Pollution Control Board (SPCB)-authorized disposal facilities, strictly adhering to the Hazardous and Other Wastes (Management and Transboundary Movement) Rules, 2016.

Treatment, Storage and Disposal Facility (TSDF)

Non-recoverable hazardous wastes such as chemical sludge, spent charcoal, distillation residue, and contaminated hazardous packaging are transported to TSDFs for final disposal. These facilities employ scientifically validated treatment methods including:

High-temperature incineration (1100–1300°C) for safe destruction of hazardous waste streams like spent solvents, contaminated PPE, and biohazardous residues.
Secure engineered landfilling for inorganic and non-degradable hazardous solid wastes such as filter cakes, inorganic sludges, and ash.

Prior to dispatch, all hazardous wastes are pre-segregated, labelled, and analysed for critical parameters including calorific value, moisture content, and chemical composition to ensure selection of the most appropriate TSDF treatment pathway.

Process Parameter Optimization: Operational parameters such as reaction temperature, pH, mixing speed, and retention time are optimized by process engineers to minimize the formation of hazardous by-products. This practice reduces both emissions and downstream treatment requirements.
In-Process Recycling and Reuse: Solvent recycling and recovery of intermediate streams are actively pursued within production cycles. This not only curbs waste generation but also contributes to cost savings and improved material efficiency.
Standardized Operating Protocols: Well-defined SOPs and process checklists guide the precise use of chemicals, including sequence of addition, concentration limits, and safety precautions. These controls reduce the risk of excessive chemical dosing or variability in output.
Continuous Real-Time Monitoring: Automated monitoring systems are installed across critical control points in the manufacturing line to ensure that process variables remain within defined thresholds, thus preventing unintended emissions or unsafe conditions.
Filtration and Contaminant Isolation: Simple but effective techniques such as sedimentation, filtration, or decantation are employed wherever feasible to separate toxic components from aqueous or organic waste streams before they are mixed or discharged.
Onsite Pre-Treatment Techniques: Select toxic by-products undergo preliminary treatments such as neutralization, oxidation, or dilution at the source. These steps help reduce the overall hazard classification of waste prior to final disposal.

Praveen Laboratories recognizes water as a vital and limited resource. As a pharmaceutical R&D facility, the responsible management of water use and wastewater discharge is critical to our sustainability goals and environmental compliance. This SOP outlines our structured approach to water use, quality monitoring, conservation, and management of risks associated with water use and contamination especially with regards to pharmaceutical actives (APIs).

Ensure efficient and minimal use of water across operations.
Monitor, analyze, and manage wastewater discharge responsibly in the absence of an ETP.
Implement mechanisms for API capture and containment at the source.
Integrate water audits and quality checks into operational routines.
Comply with local, state, and national water regulations.

body.text: Process Cooling and Thermal Systems
Regular maintenance is performed on chillers, water baths, and heat exchangers to ensure optimal performance, prevent water loss, and maintain energy efficiency.

steps.heading: Leak Monitoring and Immediate Repair Protocol

body.text: Moisture sensors and manual checks help detect leaks early. All leaks are logged and repaired within 24 hours to reduce water waste and system disruptions.
Cooling systems operate on a closed-loop basis to prevent wastewater discharge and allow consistent, contamination-free thermal regulation.
Cooling intensity is automatically adjusted based on the real-time thermal load of equipment or batches, saving both water and energy.
Water-saving technologies like air-cooled chillers, dry cooling systems, and hybrid models are used to reduce dependence on water-based systems.
Energy-efficient technologies such as VFDs, insulation, and condensate reuse help reduce both water consumption and power usage in cooling operations.
Daily and monthly performance logs are maintained to monitor usage, detect inefficiencies, and guide continuous improvements in water and energy management.
Pre-treatment of process wastewater containing API residues is carried out using:

Activated carbon filters
pH neutralization tanks

Solvent-laden liquid waste is segregated at the source, stored in dedicated containers, and handed over to SPCB-authorized hazardous waste handlers for incineration or specialized disposal.
After pre-treatment, all wastewater is routed to the in-house Sewage Treatment Plant (STP), where biological and mechanical treatment processes are employed to reduce organic load, suspended solids, and residual chemicals.
The treated effluent from the STP is then transferred to a Common Effluent Treatment Plant (CETP) for final treatment and disposal, ensuring compliance with CPCB and local pollution control norms.
Greywater, such as RO reject and washwater from hand washing stations, is collected separately and reused for non-critical utility applications, such as toilet flushing and floor cleaning, reducing freshwater demand.
We maintain formal agreements with authorized off-site CETP operators, and regular effluent sampling and analysis is conducted to ensure that discharge parameters remain within permissible limits.

No untreated or treated industrial effluent, laboratory wastewater, or cleaning runoff is permitted to be discharged directly into the soil, unlined drains, or groundwater bodies. This is in strict adherence to regulatory mandates and environmental best practices.
All effluent generated is managed through designated collection systems, ensuring complete containment and routing to authorized disposal or treatment mechanisms.
Dedicated containment trays are strategically installed beneath all chemical storage racks, reagent shelving, and experimental workbenches to catch accidental leaks or spills.
Quick-response spill kits are positioned in key areas for immediate containment and neutralization of hazardous substances.
All containment infrastructures, including trays and absorbent barriers, undergo routine inspection and maintenance to ensure functional integrity.
Borewell usage is monitored monthly and groundwater levels are tracked annually.
Rainwater percolation pits and storm water drains are maintained to support aquifer recharge.

sections.title: Removal of Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients (APIs) from Wastewater

blocks.text: We have adopt a robust, multi-layered approach to eliminate trace APIs from wastewater and prevent pharmaceutical pollution of surface water and soil ecosystems. The strategy involves source-level isolation, advanced treatment technologies, controlled disposal, and R&D-based innovation.

sections.title: Removal of Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients (APIs) from Wastewater

body.text:
Streams that contain APIs or intermediates—such as wash water from reactor cleaning, filtrates from product drying, and mother liquors—are identified and segregated at the point of generation to prevent dilution or mixing with greywater or STP-bound utility wastewater.
API-containing waste is not routed to general drains or biological treatment plants due to its persistent and potentially toxic nature.

Granular Activated Carbon (GAC) Columns are deployed to adsorb organic pharmaceutical residues from high-risk liquid streams. Spent GAC media is periodically regenerated or disposed of through authorized vendors.
Multi-barrier polishing units, combining activated carbon with ion exchange resins and sediment filters, are being piloted to enhance final discharge quality.

All API-bearing waste is collected in designated leak-proof containers, each labeled with:
API type
Concentration
Volume
Generation source
Containers are barcoded and tracked using the Waste Manifest Management System (WMMS), ensuring full traceability.
This waste is stored temporarily in a dedicated hazardous chemical storage zone and handed over to TSDF (Treatment, Storage and Disposal Facility) vendors approved under the Hazardous Waste Rules.

The company's R&D division is actively investigating advanced destruction technologies such as:
Biological degradation using engineered microbes that can metabolize API structures in aerobic or anaerobic bioreactors.
Photocatalysis using TiO₂-based materials, which when exposed to UV light, degrade complex pharmaceutical molecules into less harmful components.
Collaborative studies with academic institutions and environmental laboratories are underway to validate these approaches and assess their viability for scale-up.

All practices align with national guidance on API discharge control, including:

sops.title: Air Emissions and Environmental Nuisance Control

blocks.text: At Praveen Laboratories, maintaining clean air within and around our facility is a core aspect of our environmental and occupational safety responsibilities. Although our operations are laboratory-scale and non-industrial, emissions of particulate matter, vapors, noise, and odors are managed with the same diligence as in large-scale facilities. This SOP outlines preventive strategies and control technologies adopted to mitigate atmospheric emissions, laboratory odors, and noise pollution, ensuring compliance and community well-being.

Prevent emissions of volatile organic compounds (VOCs), fine particulates, and chemical vapors.
Monitor indoor and ambient air quality periodically.
Implement quiet operation practices and minimize equipment noise at boundaries.
Mitigate nuisance odors using lab-scale filtration and ventilation systems.
Maintain full compliance with applicable CPCB, SPCB, and occupational hygiene norms.
This SOP applies to:

rows: Develops monitoring programs and evaluates emission risks.
Enforce air handling protocols and ensure fume hood use compliance.
Maintains filtration units, exhaust fans, and noise insulation infrastructure.
Ensure correct usage of fume hoods and odor control practices.

body.text: Multi-stage wet scrubbers are installed on distillation units and reactor vents, specifically designed to neutralize acid gases (HCl, SO₂) and water-soluble emissions generated during synthesis processes. The scrubbing efficiency is verified through pH and TDS monitoring of effluent streams.

Closed charging systems and sealed reaction vessels are used during solvent-intensive operations. These systems include nitrogen blanketing and vapor balancing lines that loop back displaced vapors to condensers or solvent recovery units.

Dedicated vapor adsorption chambers with granular activated carbon (GAC) columns are deployed at high-risk VOC emission zones such as solvent storage yards, chromatographic purification areas, and liquid transfer bays.

Leak Detection and Repair (LDAR) rounds are conducted monthly using photoionization detectors (PIDs) and infrared thermography to identify micro-leaks in pipe flanges, agitator seals, and flexible hoses. Identified leaks are logged and closed within a 48-hour corrective action cycle.
Combustion emissions from boilers and hot oil generators are controlled via low-NOx burners, and fuel quality is monitored to maintain sulfur levels within permitted limits.

Stack chimneys are designed for optimal dispersion, with minimum height standards (as per CPCB guidelines) and inline sampling ports for stack monitoring. Emissions are routinely tested by NABL-accredited labs.

CEMS (Continuous Emission Monitoring Systems) are operational on major stacks to track SOx, NOx, CO, and particulate matter. Alert thresholds are set, triggering immediate shutdown protocols if emission limits are approached.

Preventive maintenance of APC (Air Pollution Control) equipment is scheduled quarterly, covering blower calibration, duct inspections, and demister pad cleaning to avoid backpressure and capture inefficiencies.

Ambient Air Quality Monitoring (AAQM) is conducted at four boundary locations to track PM2.5, PM10, VOCs, and ammonia. Trends are reviewed monthly and compared with NAAQS standards to ensure negligible off-site impact.

Baghouse Dust Collectors with HEPA-grade filters are installed on fluid bed dryers, micronizers, and API blending systems. These units operate at >99.97% filtration efficiency for PM₂.₅, ensuring worker safety and clean air discharge in enclosed production zones.

steps.heading: Wet Scrubbing Systems with Packed Bed Columns

body.text: Wet Scrubbing Systems with Packed Bed Columns are connected to reactors and neutralization tanks to capture particulate-bound vapors and aerosols generated during acid-base reactions or granulation. Scrubbing media is changed based on pressure drop indicators and pH variance.

Electrostatic Precipitators (ESPs) are integrated with boiler stacks and thermal oxidizer exhausts, effectively removing submicron particles (<1 µm) through dual-stage charging and collection plates. Particle loading and removal efficiency are reviewed during every quarterly EHS audit.

Continuous Particulate Monitoring: PM₁₀ and PM₂.₅ sensors are placed in HVAC ducts and ambient monitoring points. Alarm-linked control panels alert operators to abnormal emission surges, prompting immediate containment or system shutdown.

Preventive Maintenance and Calibration: All baghouses, scrubbers, and ESPs follow a preventive maintenance schedule, including daily pulse-jet cleaning, filter inspection, motor checks, and airflow balance calibration to ensure sustained efficiency.

sections.title: VOC, SO₂, NOₓ, and Heavy Metal Emission Mitigation

body.text: Continuous Emission Monitoring Systems (CEMS) are installed on all critical stacks associated with distillation columns, solvent recovery units, and utility boilers. These systems continuously track real-time concentrations of VOCs, SOx, NOx, CO, and CO₂.

Ambient Air Quality Monitoring Stations (AAQMS) are established at facility perimeters in upwind and downwind locations to capture comprehensive data on local air quality trends. Monitored pollutants include VOCs, NOx, SOx, CO, and PM, and results are reviewed weekly by the EHS department.

Third-Party Manual Stack Testing is performed quarterly on all major emission sources, including process reactors, hot oil systems, and incinerators. Accredited laboratories conduct these tests to measure stack concentrations of SO₂, NOx, CO, and total VOCs. All results are certified and included in annual environmental disclosures.

Real-Time Data Analytics & Alarming: All monitored pollutants, including CO₂ and VOCs, are analyzed using in-house software that flags trends and auto-generates alarms when levels approach pre-defined thresholds. This enables immediate root cause identification and activation of corrective actions, such as flow rate adjustments or process halts.

VOC Capture and Mitigation: VOC emissions from solvent handling, extraction, and purification operations are minimized using vapor balancing systems, nitrogen blanketing, and activated carbon absorbers. Based on real-time monitoring, operational practices are dynamically adjusted to mitigate fugitive releases.

steps.heading: Routine Calibration & Maintenance of Monitoring Equipment

body.text: Routine Calibration & Maintenance of Monitoring Equipment: CEMS and AAQMS devices are calibrated monthly using certified gas standards and documented under the instrumentation quality management system. Preventive maintenance is conducted by OEM-trained technicians to ensure data accuracy and reliability.

steps.heading: Monthly Compliance Review by Environmental Management Team

body.text: Monthly Compliance Review by Environmental Management Team: Emission trends and exceedance alerts are reviewed by a cross-functional environmental task force. Root cause analyses, mitigation plans, and improvement actions are tracked through a centralized Environmental Performance Dashboard.

Regulatory Reporting & Disclosure: Comprehensive emission reports, covering pollutant loads, stack test summaries, and CEMS data logs, are compiled annually and submitted to the State Pollution Control Board (SPCB) and CPCB. Reports include emissions of SOx, NOx, VOCs, CO, and CO₂, along with details of control systems and performance efficiency.

Air curtains at lab entrances reduce cross-contamination of air between sections.

rows: Replaced all fluorescent and halogen fixtures with LED lighting, incorporating motion sensors in low-traffic areas.

Replaced legacy refrigerators and deep freezers with BEE 4-star rated or Energy Star-compliant lab models.

Power-intensive processes (e.g., distillation or synthesis) shifted to modular, digitally controlled systems for precise energy input.
Regular maintenance schedules enforced for compressors, motors, and utility pumps to reduce operational load.

Transitioned backup generator fuel from high-sulfur diesel to low-emission biodiesel blends (B10-B20), reducing particulate and SOx emissions.
Replaced gas-based laboratory burners with electric hotplates or induction systems in general-use areas.
Hot water systems for staff facilities shifted to solar-assisted heating units.
Electric Forklifts and Trolleys in Warehousing Operations: Battery-powered forklifts have replaced LPG/diesel models within raw material and packaging storage areas to minimize indoor air pollution and reduce fossil fuel dependency.
Facility Lighting Shift to Solar + LED Systems: Outdoor security lighting and perimeter lights were connected to rooftop solar power with integrated battery storage. Interior areas were fitted with LED panels, reducing reliance on grid electricity generated through coal-based sources.
Fuel Switch in Laboratory Drying Ovens: Gas-fired drying ovens were replaced with programmable electric ovens with precision controls, eliminating combustion-based heat sources and improving safety in sensitive R&D environments.

blocks.text:
Heat exchange coils integrated with HVAC systems to pre-warm incoming fresh air using exhaust stream, thereby reducing energy needed for temperature conditioning.
Closed-loop chilled water systems in use for analytical instruments to reclaim and reuse thermal load efficiently.

Waste heat generated by air compressors in the utilities section is captured and redirected for pre-heating process water used in cleaning and rinsing cycles.

sops.title: Sensitive Transaction Approval and Management Protocol

blocks.text: Praveen Laboratories is committed to executing all sensitive transactions with integrity, transparency, and regulatory alignment. This SOP defines the formalized process for identifying, evaluating, and approving transactions that may involve financial risk, reputational exposure, or ethical concerns. These protocols are designed to protect the organization's interests and promote a culture of accountability.

To establish a standardized and traceable approach for handling sensitive transactions.

To streamline the approval process while maintaining thorough oversight.

blocks.text: This protocol applies to all personnel involved in initiating, reviewing, or authorizing sensitive transactions. body.text: Every sensitive transaction begins with the initiator—an employee, department head, or project team—submitting a comprehensive transaction proposal. The proposal must clearly articulate the transaction's purpose, strategic justification, potential benefits, and associated risks. It must include supporting documentation such as draft contracts, cost breakdowns, market intelligence, risk assessments, and stakeholder analysis. No transaction proceeds without this initial documentation being complete and verified.

Upon submission, the proposal undergoes a departmental-level evaluation led by the respective Department Head. The objective is to ensure the transaction aligns with functional objectives, complies with internal norms, and does not present immediate red flags. This review emphasizes operational feasibility, alignment with budgets, and ethical neutrality. Constructive feedback is provided where necessary, and only proposals that meet all department-level expectations are forwarded to Finance and Legal for advanced scrutiny.

Any transaction presenting unresolved legal issues or ethical concerns is escalated for higher-level review or rejection. The compliance team flags any perceived irregularities and documents remedial actions.

sops.title: Confidential Data Management and record retention

blocks.text: At Praveen Laboratories Pvt. Ltd., we are firmly committed to protecting all confidential information and managing organizational records responsibly. This SOP defines the processes and responsibilities for handling, storing, and disposing of sensitive data in accordance with applicable legal obligations and internal operational standards. It ensures secure data governance practices throughout the data lifecycle.

To obtain informed and explicit consent from all stakeholders before processing, retaining, or sharing their confidential data.
To ensure robust protection of third-party information using strong digital security measures such as encryption and multi-factor authentication, alongside comprehensive physical safeguards.
To maintain a clearly defined and legally compliant data retention schedule aligned with statutory, financial, and regulatory requirements.
To promote transparency by proactively informing stakeholders about how their data is collected, used, stored, and shared.
To establish internal controls that strictly limit unauthorized access to sensitive data across all departments and functions.
To periodically review and enhance data management protocols in line with changes in regulations and business needs.
To provide well-defined support channels to address stakeholder queries related to data privacy and record handling.
To ensure that records are securely destroyed once their prescribed retention period has elapsed, using methods that prevent recovery or misuse.

This SOP is applicable to all personnel of Praveen Laboratories Pvt. Ltd., including full-time employees, contractors, consultants, and third-party service providers involved in handling any form of confidential, operational, customer, or business data. It covers both digital and physical data formats and applies across all company sites—including head offices, branch facilities, R&D centers, production units, and remote work locations. The procedure supports compliance with internal policies, sectoral regulations, and international standards under both normal operations and emergency conditions.

body.text: Consent forms issued by Praveen Laboratories Pvt. Ltd. clearly outline the purpose, scope, and duration of data processing. These forms are written in plain language to ensure stakeholders fully understand how their information will be handled, including the involvement of any third parties. Each form also highlights the stakeholder’s rights, including their ability to withdraw consent at any time.

Consent is collected through various secure platforms, including company portals, mobile apps, and in-person engagements. Each instance is recorded with a timestamp and stored safely, enabling a traceable audit trail and ensuring accessibility across systems.

All consents are recorded within our centralized data systems, which allow controlled access and real-time tracking. Role-based permissions are enforced to prevent unauthorized modification and ensure compliance with data protection laws.

Stakeholder consents are periodically reviewed to ensure they remain valid. When changes to our data practices occur, stakeholders are informed and asked to reaffirm or update their consent accordingly.
Stakeholders may withdraw their consent at any time through a simple and defined procedure. All requests are logged, processed without delay, and acknowledged to the concerned individual.

We engage stakeholders through educational materials such as policy updates, FAQs, and training sessions to keep them informed about how their data is managed and their rights under applicable regulations.

The Compliance Team conducts routine checks to verify that consent collection and management practices align with legal and internal standards. Any gaps identified are addressed promptly through corrective actions.

sections.title: Operational Process for Consulting and Informing Stakeholders

body.text: Praveen Laboratories provides stakeholders with clear and accessible information about how their data is collected, used, stored, and shared. This is communicated via the company website, formal emails, and direct consultations, enhancing understanding and trust.

Detailed data handling documentation is maintained and made available to stakeholders upon request. This includes our policies on collection, retention, sharing, and disposal, offering full transparency into our data management framework.
We have dedicated support channels in place to address data-related inquiries. Trained personnel provide timely, accurate responses to any concerns raised by customers, employees, or partners.

Our consent and communication practices are regularly reviewed and updated to remain aligned with evolving legal and operational requirements. Any significant updates are communicated promptly to relevant stakeholders.

Consistent with our transparency-first approach, we use multiple communication methods—including digital platforms and direct meetings—to keep stakeholders informed about the lifecycle of their data. This encourages mutual understanding and accountability.

Access to sensitive information is strictly governed through role-based access permissions. Only authorized personnel with a verified need are granted access, ensuring controlled exposure of confidential data such as client information, supplier data, and operational inputs.
Our digital infrastructure employs multiple security layers—encryption, secure servers, and multi-factor authentication—to prevent unauthorized access.

In addition to digital safeguards, strong physical security measures are enforced at all locations where confidential records are stored. These areas, including server rooms and record archives, are protected using biometric access controls, access ID cards, and CCTV surveillance, with entry limited to pre-approved individuals.

Employees are trained routinely on data protection protocols and their roles in maintaining confidentiality. Audit logs, intrusion detection systems, and real-time alerts are in place to monitor any anomalies or potential data breaches, enabling prompt action when needed.

sections.title: Internal Controls to Restrict Data Access

body.text: Our IT environment features advanced security protocols including multi-factor authentication, user-specific access control, and continuous threat monitoring. All access is logged, reviewed, and restricted strictly to employees whose duties require data interaction. Software updates and vulnerability patches are applied regularly.

Entry to physical data repositories is tightly regulated. Access badges, biometric scanners, and 24/7 video monitoring systems are used to enforce restricted access. Only designated personnel may enter these areas, reducing the risk of unauthorized handling.

Regular audits—both internal and external—are conducted to evaluate access control effectiveness and detect vulnerabilities. Audit trails are maintained through system-generated logs and are reviewed frequently to identify suspicious access patterns or policy violations.

The purpose of this procedure is to define and institutionalize a structured, transparent, and organization-wide approach for conducting internal assessments at Praveen Laboratories. These assessments help evaluate the effectiveness of internal controls, policy implementation, and regulatory compliance, while promoting operational integrity and continuous improvement across all key functional areas.
This SOP applies to all departments and operational units of Praveen Laboratories and governs the conduct of annual internal assessments on key thematic areas, including but not limited to:

Corruption and Anti-Bribery Controls
Labor Practices and Human Rights
Occupational Health & Safety (OHS)
Information Security and Data Confidentiality
Discrimination, Harassment, and Whistleblower Protections
Employee Satisfaction survey on Working Condition
These assessments are aligned with applicable legal requirements, ISO standards, client expectations, and internal policies.

body.text: Each year in January, the Internal Audit Coordinator prepares the Annual Internal Assessment Plan, identifying the thematic areas to be assessed across the organization. The plan is reviewed and approved by the Senior Management Team and aligned with regulatory calendars, client expectations, and audit preparedness needs.
A standardized Internal Assessment Questionnaire or Form is developed for each focus area. The forms are reviewed and updated annually in collaboration with functional experts and include:

Objective questions (Yes/No/NA)
Subjective questions (scored on 1–5 scale)
Comments and observations fields
Declaration of accuracy and approval by the responsible manager

The finalized assessment forms are distributed to department heads and relevant staff members via email or internal platforms. Employees are informed about the importance of timely and accurate participation. A deadline of 10–15 working days is set for submission. Anonymous formats are used for assessments related to corruption, discrimination, or whistleblower safety.

Upon collection, all completed assessments are reviewed by the Internal Audit Coordinator and cross-functional reviewers. Clarifications are requested where inconsistencies or missing data are observed. Each department is scored on key parameters such as policy awareness, compliance rate, documentation completeness, and risk exposure.
Findings are categorized as:

Fully Compliant
Partially Compliant
Non-Compliant
Detailed observations are supported by audit trails, records, or visual evidence where applicable.
A department-wise compliance report is prepared and shared within 15 working days of assessment closure. The report highlights:

Compliance percentage
Gaps and non-conformances
Observations and commendable practices
Recommended corrective and preventive actions
Each department receives a tailored scorecard and executive summary.

For any non-compliance or identified weakness, the concerned department must prepare and submit a Corrective and Preventive Action (CAPA) Plan within 10 working days. All CAPA items are logged in a centralized tracker and assigned clear timelines and responsibilities.
Progress updates are monitored monthly by the Internal Audit Coordinator, and critical gaps are escalated to the Compliance Officer or Senior Management.
At the end of each assessment cycle, a consolidated Internal Assessment Summary Report is presented during the annual Management Review Meeting. The summary includes:

Overall compliance trends
High-risk areas requiring strategic focus

blocks.text: All internal assessments—particularly those involving sensitive issues such as corruption, harassment, or whistleblower concerns—are treated as confidential. Access to completed assessments and supporting evidence is restricted to the Internal Audit Coordinator, Compliance Officer, and Senior Management.

The internal assessment process is reviewed annually to incorporate lessons learned, feedback from departments, and external audit recommendations. Assessment formats, scoring logic, and timelines may be refined to improve relevance, clarity, and effectiveness. Training and awareness sessions are conducted annually to improve the quality and engagement level of participants.

Praveen Laboratories is dedicated to upholding the highest ethical standards in its business practices, especially when working with third-party entities such as suppliers, service providers, vendors, and contractors. This SOP outlines the procedures to assess, monitor, and manage third-party compliance with ethical, legal, and sustainability benchmarks.
This procedure ensures:

Responsible Third-Party Onboarding: A defined framework for evaluating new partners' ethical alignment.
Risk Mitigation: Identification and control of risks related to unethical practices like bribery, unsafe labor, and data breaches.
Promotion of Sustainable Practices: Verification that suppliers align with human rights norms, labor regulations, and environmental values.
Data Security Assurance: Confirmation that data privacy safeguards and information security standards are upheld.
Transparency in Record-Keeping: Secure documentation of assessments, audits, and decisions.
Ongoing Ethical Oversight: Regular assessments and incident management mechanisms to ensure sustained compliance.

This SOP applies to all departments at Praveen Laboratories involved in engaging third parties, including procurement, administration, operations, and finance. It applies to both new and ongoing engagements.

body.text: Integrity & Anti-Corruption, Fair Labor & Human Rights, Environmental Stewardship, Information Security & Data Protection and Occupational Health & Safety are the initial review areas.

substeps.text: Integrity & Anti-Corruption: Review for past allegations or violations involving bribery or unethical inducements. Confirm adherence to anti-corruption policies and applicable laws.
Fair Labor & Human Rights: Check compliance with child labor and forced labor laws. Examine working condition standards and employee protection policies.
Environmental Stewardship: Review waste management, emissions control, and certification (e.g., ISO 14001). Assess commitment to environmental best practices.
Information Security & Data Protection: Verify policies for handling confidential and sensitive data. Require industry-recognized certification (e.g., ISO 27001 or equivalent).
Occupational Health & Safety: Confirm third party follows safety laws and implements adequate safety protocols for its staff.

All third-party engagement decisions are made by a cross-functional review panel including Admin, Procurement, and Finance leads.
Final approvals are documented in the central supplier register with associated due diligence findings.

Annual On-Site Reviews: Conducted to verify adherence to ethical, safety, and environmental standards.
Self-Assessment Forms: Required yearly from each vendor, reviewed by procurement and HR.
Random Spot Checks: Conducted if red flags emerge or if significant operational changes occur.
Ethical Incidents: Third parties must report any data breach, safety incident, or human rights violation within 24 hours.

Incident Logging: Every reported issue is recorded in the Third-Party Ethics Case Register.
Action Planning: Mitigation steps are agreed upon with the vendor and tracked for resolution.
Escalation Protocol: High-risk or unresolved cases are escalated to the Ethics Compliance Team and may lead to contract termination.

All ethical review records, checklists, correspondence, incident logs, and certifications are digitized and stored in the vendor management system.
Records are retained for a minimum of 5 years or as required by applicable legal statutes.
